comments.proportion: Cell-type fractions of the model. Anatomical interneuron fractions are 7-15% of neurons; a model can over-represent interneurons on purpose, which should then be stated.
comments.cells_per_volume: Model volume = region declared in the input (NetMorph disc) or the convex hull of the somata; a thin disc with a few hundred cells is far below tissue density unless the region is matched to it. No CA3 number was found.
comments.length.axon.pyramidal: A real CA3 pyramidal axon (150-500 mm) lies mostly outside any local patch, so this is not a like-for-like comparison; the model axon is the locally grown part.
comments.length.axon.interneuron: Slice values are lower bounds (cut axons).
comments.length.dendrite.pyramidal: CA3 values depend on position along the CA3 axis (Ishizuka 1995).
comments.reach_max: Spherical range = farthest arbor point from the soma centre, per cell; the table shows the mean and median over cells and the max over cells.
comments.reach_max.axon.interneuron: Literature gives lateral extent (full width) of CA1 PV basket axons; half of it is used as a derived reach estimate.
comments.targets: Distinct partner cells inside the model only. Whole-cell numbers in tissue (e.g. >1500 pyramidal targets per basket cell) include cells outside any patch.
comments.conn_prob: Connected ordered pairs / possible ordered pairs inside the model. The Ecker 2022 values are model parameters, not anatomy.
comments.syn_per_pair: Contacts per connected pair (one contact per synapse, not per receptor).
comments.syn_dendrite: Contacts received by the cell from cells inside the model only; tissue numbers include extrinsic afferents.
comments.ball_index: Heat-map check: neurite length density near the region centre (r < R/3) divided by the density near the rim (2R/3 <= r < R), inside the slab. Spatially uniform neurite gives about 1; a value far above 1 means the arbors pile up in the middle (an 'axon ball').

notes: NetMorph node files carry no radii: only length density is available (no volume fraction).
ball_index.axon.interneuron = 115.2: the neurite is 115.2x denser near the centre than near the rim (axon/dendrite ball).
ball_index.axon.pyramidal = 133.0: the neurite is 133.0x denser near the centre than near the rim (axon/dendrite ball).
ball_index.axon.all = 127.0: the neurite is 127.0x denser near the centre than near the rim (axon/dendrite ball).

comments.proportion: Cell-type fractions of the model. Anatomical interneuron fractions are 7-15% of neurons; a model can over-represent interneurons on purpose, which should then be stated.
comments.cells_per_volume: Model volume = region declared in the input (NetMorph disc) or the convex hull of the somata; a thin disc with a few hundred cells is far below tissue density unless the region is matched to it. No CA3 number was found.
comments.length.axon.pyramidal: A real CA3 pyramidal axon (150-500 mm) lies mostly outside any local patch, so this is not a like-for-like comparison; the model axon is the locally grown part.
comments.length.axon.interneuron: Slice values are lower bounds (cut axons).
comments.length.dendrite.pyramidal: CA3 values depend on position along the CA3 axis (Ishizuka 1995).
comments.reach_max: Spherical range = farthest arbor point from the soma centre, per cell; the table shows the mean and median over cells and the max over cells.
comments.reach_max.axon.interneuron: Literature gives lateral extent (full width) of CA1 PV basket axons; half of it is used as a derived reach estimate.
comments.targets: Distinct partner cells inside the model only. Whole-cell numbers in tissue (e.g. >1500 pyramidal targets per basket cell) include cells outside any patch.
comments.conn_prob: Connected ordered pairs / possible ordered pairs inside the model. The Ecker 2022 values are model parameters, not anatomy.
comments.syn_per_pair: Contacts per connected pair (one contact per synapse, not per receptor).
comments.syn_dendrite: Contacts received by the cell from cells inside the model only; tissue numbers include extrinsic afferents.
comments.ball_index: Heat-map check: neurite length density near the region centre (r < R/3) divided by the density near the rim (2R/3 <= r < R), inside the slab. Spatially uniform neurite gives about 1; a value far above 1 means the arbors pile up in the middle (an 'axon ball').

notes: NetMorph node files carry no radii: only length density is available (no volume fraction).
